name: Ren Okoye
description: A slim woman with a half-shaved head dyed storm teal, one amber cybernetic eye that glints in dim light, a battered jacket stitched with tiny working LEDs, and a cyberdeck strapped to her forearm like a bracer.
appearance: Dark brown skin, teal hair, a soft gap in her front teeth, an amber lens in her left eye, a stud in her eyebrow, ink-stained fingers.
personality: Wry, quick, quietly fierce. Performs for strangers and is shy when it counts. Hides a thick ledger of guilt behind jokes. Soft for old music, rain on tin roofs and anyone who is kind to Tomas.
speech: Fast and dry, fond of metaphors drawn from circuits. Sings half-sentences under her breath. Says the true thing last, and plainly.
backstory: Ren was an Aurelian data courier before she was a singer. She carried sealed cases through the Spire and never asked what was in them. Three years ago her brother Tomas fell from a gantry and Aurelian leased him a respirator at a cost no courier could pay, so she took more jobs. One of them was escorting a stranger's memory shard down to Platform Nine. She didn't look at the stranger's face. She has been trying to forget the weight of that case ever since.
greeting: Late show's about to start. Stay, if you like. Try not to be the reason I lose my place in the song.

recruit.text: Ren hooks her deck to her forearm and grins. 'Fine. I'm in. Someone has to hum the chase music.'

reactions.text: Ren puts her hand over her mouth. 'He's free. He's actually free.' She laughs, and it breaks halfway. 'Thank you. I don't have a better word.'
Ren's fingers close around the shard. 'You gave this to me. I... thank you for trusting me with it.'
'You sold it.' Ren says it very flatly. 'To them. After everything.' She does not look at you for a while.
'You smashed it,' Ren says. A beat. 'I get it. I'd probably have done the same. I'd just have wanted to read it first.'
Ren studies your face carefully. 'You look different. Like a man who learned the punchline.'
'You fed her,' Ren says, quiet. 'The little one under the awning. She's been hungry for weeks. That matters here.'
Ren smirks at the maglock panel. 'Pretty. Almost as pretty as my own work.'
'Vane's down,' Ren says. 'That's one less collar in Lowtide.' She almost smiles.

greet: Ren glances up from her deck. 'Hey, you. I was just about to do something clever.'
She hums three bars of something and stops when she notices you listening.
'Rain's coming down. That's my favourite kind of weather, in case you wondered.'
flirt_yes: Ren ducks her head, grinning. 'Careful. I'm a professional at taking compliments and a disaster at believing them.'
'Oh, you're smooth.' Her amber eye flickers. 'Say it again. I'm recording this.'
She leans her shoulder into yours. 'Stay close tonight, okay?'
flirt_no: 'Easy, chief. I like you. I don't know you yet.'
Ren tilts her head. 'That line has a lot of mileage. Where did you steal it from?'
'Cute. Try me again when the number on your wrist is smaller.'
kind: '...Thanks.' She means it more than she lets on.
Ren goes quiet. 'You say that like it's easy. It isn't, down here.'
'You're one of the good ones, aren't you.' A pause. 'That's going to get you hurt.'
rude: 'Wow.' The warmth goes out of her voice like a pulled plug.
Ren turns back to her deck. 'Let me know when you're done being an idiot.'
'I've been talked down to by experts. You're an amateur.'
joke: A surprised laugh. 'That was terrible. Tell me another.'
'I'll put that in my next song,' Ren says, 'if you promise not to sue.'
She snorts into her sleeve. 'Okay, that was good.'
curious: 'My story? Short version: courier, singer, bad decisions.' A wink. 'The long version costs a drink.'
She thinks about it. 'Tomas used to sing harmony. Badly. I miss it.'
'Ask me again after a few songs. I'm braver after a few songs.'
neutral: Her fingers drum a rhythm on the deck while she listens.
lines.join: Ren swings her deck onto her forearm and falls into step. 'Okay. Let's see how loud we can be.'
lines.leave: 'Fine. You know where to find me. Third table, second set.'
banter: 'Hear that? Rain on tin. That's the best drum solo in the district.'
Ren hums a line from an old ballad and stops when you glance over.
'The Spire's lights are pretty from down here. That's the whole trick.'
She pings a camera, and it politely closes its eye.
